sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **August Declaration 1917**: The bedrock of the Act, promising 'responsible government' in India.
• **Dyarchy**: The core mechanism of 'Double Rule' in provinces, dividing subjects into 'Reserved' and 'Transferred'.
• **Bicameralism**: Introduction of a two-house legislature at the Centre (Council of State and Legislative Assembly).
• **Key Metric**: Franchise was limited based on property, tax, or education, covering only ~3% of the population.

items.definition: A dual system of government where provincial subjects were split into Reserved (Governor-controlled) and Transferred (Minister-controlled).
Extended the 1909 principle to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians, and Europeans, deepening the 'Divide and Rule' policy.
A new office created in London to take over some functions of the Secretary of State for India.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Public Service Commission**: Established a Central Public Service Commission in 1926 for recruiting civil servants.
• **Budgetary Separation**: Separated provincial budgets from the central budget for the first time.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Financial control remained with the Governor; Ministers had no control over finance or bureaucracy.
• **Solutions**: Led to the demand for a Statutory Commission (Simon Commission) to review the working of the Act.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'B-I-D-E' (Bicameralism, Indian participation, Dyarchy, Extension of communal electorates).
• **Decoded Meaning**: B: Bicameralism at Centre; I: Indian participation increased; D: Dyarchy in Provinces; E: Extension of communal franchise.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Responsible Government' (1919) with 'Provincial Autonomy' (1935). 1919 introduced Dyarchy; 1935 abolished Dyarchy and introduced Provincial Autonomy.
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'The Act was a half-hearted attempt at devolution' to critique the limited nature of the reforms.

keyTakeaways: Dyarchy was the most significant feature, creating a split executive in provinces.
The Act introduced direct elections and bicameralism at the central level.
It failed to satisfy nationalist aspirations, leading to the Non-Cooperation Movement.
